text.title: HealthTech FHIR BA Pack Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when producing a HealthTech FHIR BA pack. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action) keyed to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

failure-mode.description: Vitals, diagnoses or medications live in an application-specific JSON column; the first EHR integration or patient-access request forces a data migration.
failure-mode.detector: Data model contains clinical fields with no FHIR resource and element path in the mapping table.
failure-mode.repair: Map every clinical element to a FHIR R4/R5 resource and profile per r-clinical-elements-map-to-fhir-resources before schema work starts.

failure-mode.description: Conditions and observations are stored as typed strings or a home-grown code list; cohorts, de-identification and exchange all fail.
failure-mode.detector: `Observation.code`, `Condition.code` or medication fields without a standard code system URI, or a local enum for a concept LOINC / SNOMED CT / RxNorm already covers.
failure-mode.repair: Bind to the terminology the profile requires per r-coded-terminology-bindings; keep free text only as `.text` alongside the code.

failure-mode.description: An LLM API, error tracker or email gateway receives PHI on the strength of the vendor's compliance page; no BAA or Art. 28 agreement exists.
failure-mode.detector: Processor list entry with PHI in scope and agreement status blank, "pending" or "vendor states compliant".
failure-mode.repair: Block the flow until the agreement is signed per r-baa-or-dpa-per-processor; strip PHI from the payload if the vendor will not sign.

failure-mode.description: One checkbox covers treatment, marketing and a research dataset; the study cannot prove who consented to which version and the data must be withdrawn.
failure-mode.detector: Consent model with one record and no scope, provision, text version or IRB protocol reference.
failure-mode.repair: Model separate, versioned FHIR Consent records and attach the IRB protocol number and approval date per r-consent-as-fhir-consent-with-irb-reference.

failure-mode.description: Access logs are application rows the app can update, rotate after 90 days, and cannot be filtered by patient; an accounting-of-disclosures request cannot be answered.
failure-mode.detector: Application role with UPDATE or DELETE on the audit table, retention under six years, or no patient-id index on the log.
failure-mode.repair: Move to append-only storage with six-year retention and per-patient query per r-audit-trail-append-only-six-years.

failure-mode.description: The pack designs to HIPAA only; EU patients get a 30-day access SLA and a delete button that HIPAA-era records cannot honour.
failure-mode.detector: Overlap matrix missing the breach-clock, access, erasure or lawful-basis rows, or a row without the stricter clock named.
failure-mode.repair: Complete the minimum rows and record the stricter-of-both decision per r-hipaa-gdpr-overlap-matrix-minimum-rows.
